haiku-low.q1: The scheduler starts it daily at 02:00 UTC. It extracts replica orders rows where updated_at > last_high_water minus 2 hours.
haiku-low.q2: Bulk-import transactions can stay open up to 90 minutes, and updated_at is stamped at write time, not commit. So rows can become visible up to 90 minutes after updated_at.
haiku-low.q3: The edit changes updated_at, so a later extract picks it up. The 2-hour lookback re-reads it, and the merge upserts it, latest updated_at winning.
haiku-low.q4: The soft delete arrives as an updated row. The merge sets is_deleted = true in fact_orders. Rows are never removed from the warehouse.
haiku-low.q5: The attempt fails and the scheduler waits 15 minutes, then reruns from step 1. Up to 3 attempts total; after the third failure, on-call is paged.
haiku-low.q6: Dashboards show the previous fully committed night's data, since they read only committed fact_orders. A separate 06:00 check posts a staleness alert to #data-alerts.
haiku-low.q7: The weekly Sunday reconciliation reloads that creation day. It re-extracts by creation date and runs load and merge, so the newer version reaches the warehouse.
haiku-low.q8: Staging is deduplicated by order_id keeping the greatest updated_at. The merge overwrites a stored row only if the staged updated_at is greater than or equal to the stored one.
haiku-low.q9: Stored in etl_watermark.last_high_water. Written inside the final merge transaction, set to the greater of current value and max updated_at extracted; unchanged if empty.
haiku-low.q10: The data merge, watermark update and success mark commit in one warehouse transaction. Dashboards read only committed fact_orders, so they never see a half-loaded night.
haiku-low.q11: Staged data is wiped on the next load, so it is discarded. The retry extracts from last_high_water minus 2 hours again, since a failed attempt never moves the watermark.
haiku-low.q12: It re-reads that creation day's orders from the replica by creation date. It applies them via normal load and merge with the same upsert rule. It does not move the watermark.

sonnet.q1: The scheduler starts it at 02:00 UTC daily. It extracts rows from the Postgres read replica `orders` table where updated_at > last_high_water - 2 hours.
sonnet.q2: Bulk-import transactions can stay open up to 90 minutes, and updated_at is stamped at write time, not commit time, so the row becomes visible up to 90 minutes after its updated_at.
sonnet.q3: The edit bumps updated_at, so a later nightly extract (updated_at > watermark - 2h) picks it up, and the merge upserts it into fact_orders because the staged updated_at is >= the stored one.
sonnet.q4: A soft delete (deleted_at set) arrives as an ordinary updated row; the merge stores it in fact_orders with is_deleted = true. Rows are never removed from the warehouse.
sonnet.q5: The attempt fails and is logged as failed in etl_runs. The scheduler waits 15 minutes and reruns from step 1, at most 2 retries (3 attempts). The watermark is untouched. After the third failure, on-call is paged.
sonnet.q6: Dashboards refresh at 06:00 anyway and show only committed data, i.e. the previous night's state. The 06:00 deadline check reads etl_runs and posts a staleness alert to #data-alerts (independent of paging).
sonnet.q7: The Sunday reconciliation job: it compares count and checksum per creation day over the last 30 days between the replica and fact_orders, and reloads mismatched days by creation date through the normal load and merge.
sonnet.q8: In the merge, staging is deduplicated by order_id keeping the greatest updated_at, and the upsert into fact_orders overwrites an existing row only if the staged updated_at is >= the stored one.
sonnet.q9: In the warehouse table etl_watermark (column last_high_water, single row). It is set to the greater of its current value and the max updated_at of the extract (unchanged if the extract was empty), inside the merge transaction, at the final commit together with the data and the succeeded mark.
sonnet.q10: The merge, watermark advance and succeeded mark are one warehouse transaction, and dashboards read only fact_orders (committed data), never staging. So they see either the previous state or the new one.
sonnet.q11: Staged data is simply wiped/replaced on the next load (staging is replaced each run). The retry reruns from step 1 and extracts updated_at > last_high_water - 2 hours, with the watermark unchanged by the failed attempt.
sonnet.q12: It re-reads the mismatched day's orders from the replica by creation date (not by watermark). They go through the normal load and merge, with the same upsert rule. The watermark update is skipped, so the nightly high-water mark is not changed.
